prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, through ligand design that made amine arylation a broadly applicable reaction

statement.case_for: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling remains the case with the cleanest combination of a general, ligand-designed method, a stable mechanistic picture (amine coordination, deprotonation, C-N reductive elimination from Pd-amido complexes) and more than 25 years of independent confirmation in pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis. In one sentence for the chair's question: Heck, Negishi and Suzuki were honoured for C-C bond formation, whereas Buchwald and Hartwig solved a different mechanistic problem, the difficult C-N reductive elimination, by ligand design, and the citation should say C-N bond formation explicitly to keep it apart from 2010. Buchwald and Hartwig built the general catalytic systems independently and in parallel, so a two-name citation is exact. Kosugi's tin-amide coupling was stoichiometric in tin and narrow in scope, so he belongs in the scientific background and not in the citation. Four of eight members now prefer this configuration with identical names, which is the closest any candidate is to a majority.
statement.case_against: The 2010 cross-coupling prize remains the main criticism, and some members (Chabes, Sparr) weigh it as a novelty problem and not a maturity one; I cannot remove that by argument alone, only by a precise citation. Kosugi's priority is a real complication that the Academy would have to address in the narrative. The opposing case is B068, which has the widest ranking and opens a new modality, but its credit is split between the PROTAC and cereblon-glue strands and no degrader is yet approved.

responses.point: Brzezinski would credit the nitrogenase structure to Rees and Einsle and prefers an incomplete roster to rewarding an open mechanism, and he asks how I weigh Einsle against Seefeldt if three slots are forced.
responses.response: After your question and Somfai's caution I have to concede the structural part is not defensible as I wrote it. The honest reading of the evidence is that the first MoFe-protein structure and the carbide-containing cofactor are two crystallographic results, from Rees and from Einsle, and a one-name Rees citation misstates that. A fair B003 part would need Rees and Einsle, which with Buchwald and Hartwig exceeds the three-person limit. Seefeldt's work is biochemical and would not be my third name for a structure citation, but I will not defend a split between the two lines that the room does not support.

responses.point: Somfai doubts nitrogenase because the catalytic mechanism and N2 binding site are still being refined, and he is cautious about five credited names in a three-person split.
responses.response: I agree with the concern, and it is my own earlier uncertainty. I also thank you for the defence of the 2010 distinction, which I now use in my case. Nobody else in the room supports B003 as a second part and the attribution cannot be cut cleanly, so I withdraw it from my preferred configuration. This makes my position the same as yours, B011 alone, and I regard it as a scientific judgement on credit and maturity, not as a move to inflate a count.

responses.point: Chabes ranks C-N coupling sixth because it follows the 2010 prize and would honour an extension of a recently recognised class of reactions, while accepting it as a possible second choice.
responses.response: I accept that this is a judgement about novelty. I would answer that the novelty is in the mechanism, since the hard step in amination is the C-N reductive elimination from an amido complex, which the C-C couplings never had to solve, and the ligand classes that solved it were new. On B068, I agree that ternary-complex structures give a strong mechanistic basis, and I keep it as my first alternative. My hesitation is about the citation, not the importance: you favour Ciulli and Aili favours Handa, which shows the committee has not yet agreed what single discovery is being honoured.

responses.point: Aqvist says the 2010 concern is answered by the different mechanistic problem in amination and wants the citation to state C-N bond formation explicitly, with Kosugi in the background.
responses.response: I agree on both points and have written the citation that way. I also agree that the discovery to be honoured is the ligand-design logic that made the reaction general, not industrial use, which is a consequence. On B001, I ranked it and I understand why you keep it, but I share the view that its credit is spread over six names and that foundation-model potentials may change which contribution proves central, so I do not think it can carry a majority this year.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that C-N coupling is conceptually distinct from the 2010 prize, which depends on how precisely the citation is worded.
Whether Kosugi's tin-amide precedent needs more than a statement in the background narrative.
Whether B068 can reach a single agreed citation and three names before the vote, and whether the absence of an approved degrader should weigh against it.
Whether a nitrogenase prize can be worded safely at all while the N2 binding site and catalytic cycle are unresolved, and which structural names would be required.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal. As an electron crystallographer I may favour structural candidates such as B003 and B057, but I have withdrawn B003 from my preferred configuration. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, which does not bear on any candidate. I have no known personal or institutional tie to Buchwald, Hartwig, Kosugi or any other named candidate.
